axes.brief:
Vetted elections and an elected presidency coexist with supreme clerical authority and constrained opposition. Focused review prioritises implemented competitive renewal and effective oversight; formal powers in controlled institutions are not automatically democratic accountability.
Focused six-question reassessment: Specialist and jurist bodies constrain elected institutions within superior clerical authority. The elected and independent parliamentary premises fit only partially; popular lawmaking remains subject to religious screening rather than an autonomous public legislative mandate.
axes.counterEvidence:
The March2026 succession used the Assembly of Experts; the president, supreme leader and armed forces have different constitutional powers, so restrictions are not assigned from a generic autocracy label. The bank also credits rejection of specific unelected alternatives (experts, unions, military) and narrower formal rights. These literal answers are retained where supported; the resulting percentage is not a probability or validated democracy index. Restrictions on women inform political participation where relevant, without automatically transferring Authority vs Liberty scores.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. Specialist and jurist bodies constrain elected institutions within superior clerical authority. The elected and independent parliamentary premises fit only partially; popular lawmaking remains subject to religious screening rather than an autonomous public legislative mandate.

This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty.
